questions.question: A painter uses paint at a rate of \(4\) bundles for every \(120\) square feet of wall covered. At this rate, how many bundles of paint will he need in order to cover a wall that is \(540\) square feet?

solution.exhibit_text:
Set up a proportion:

\[\dfrac{x}{540}=\dfrac{4}{120}\]
\[120x=2{,}160\]
\[x=18\text{ bundles}\]

questions.question: A landscaper uses fertilizer at a rate of \(5\) bags for every \(150\) square feet of lawn covered. At this rate, how many bags of fertilizer will she need in order to cover a lawn that is \(480\) square feet?

solution.exhibit_text:
Set up a proportion:

\[\dfrac{x}{480}=\dfrac{5}{150}\]
\[150x=2{,}400\]
\[x=16\text{ bags}\]

questions.question: A tiler uses tiles at a rate of \(2\) boxes for every \(80\) square feet of floor covered. At this rate, how many boxes of tiles will he need in order to cover a floor that is \(360\) square feet?

solution.exhibit_text:
Set up a proportion:

\[\dfrac{x}{360}=\dfrac{2}{80}\]
\[80x=720\]
\[x=9\text{ boxes}\]

questions.question: A large circular serving tray has a radius of \(15\) centimeters. A smaller circular tray with a circumference of \(10\pi\) centimeters is placed in the center of the larger tray. What is the area of the part of the larger tray that is **not** covered by the smaller tray?

solution.exhibit_text:
The radius of the large tray is \(15\) cm. Use \(15\) cm to find the area of the large tray:

\[A=\pi r^2=\pi(15^2)=225\pi\text{ sq cm}\]

The circumference of the smaller tray is \(10\pi\) cm. Use that to find the radius, and then the area, of the smaller tray:

\[C=2\pi r\]
\[10\pi=2\pi r\]
\[r=5\]
\[A=\pi r^2=\pi(5^2)=25\pi\text{ sq cm}\]

Subtract the area of the small tray from the area of the large tray:

\[225\pi-25\pi=200\pi\text{ sq cm}\]

questions.question: A large circular garden bed has a radius of \(25\) feet. A smaller circular garden bed with a circumference of \(30\pi\) feet is placed in the center of the larger bed. What is the area of the part of the larger bed that is **not** covered by the smaller bed?

solution.exhibit_text:
The radius of the large bed is \(25\) ft. Use \(25\) ft to find the area of the large bed:

\[A=\pi r^2=\pi(25^2)=625\pi\text{ sq ft}\]

The circumference of the smaller bed is \(30\pi\) ft. Use that to find the radius, and then the area, of the smaller bed:

\[C=2\pi r\]
\[30\pi=2\pi r\]
\[r=15\]
\[A=\pi r^2=\pi(15^2)=225\pi\text{ sq ft}\]

Subtract the area of the small bed from the area of the large bed:

\[625\pi-225\pi=400\pi\text{ sq ft}\]

questions.question: A large circular rug has a radius of \(12\) feet. A smaller circular rug with a circumference of \(8\pi\) feet is placed in the center of the larger rug. What is the area of the part of the larger rug that is **not** covered by the smaller rug?

solution.exhibit_text:
The radius of the large rug is \(12\) ft. Use \(12\) ft to find the area of the large rug:

\[A=\pi r^2=\pi(12^2)=144\pi\text{ sq ft}\]

The circumference of the smaller rug is \(8\pi\) ft. Use that to find the radius, and then the area, of the smaller rug:

\[C=2\pi r\]
\[8\pi=2\pi r\]
\[r=4\]
\[A=\pi r^2=\pi(4^2)=16\pi\text{ sq ft}\]

Subtract the area of the small rug from the area of the large rug:

\[144\pi-16\pi=128\pi\text{ sq ft}\]

questions.question: Points \(X\), \(Y\), and \(Z\) are on a straight line, and \(Y\) is between \(X\) and \(Z\). Length \(\overline{YZ}=\dfrac{2}{3}\overline{XY}\), and length \(\overline{XY}=18\) centimeters. What is the length of \(\overline{XZ}\)?

solution.exhibit_text:
Since \(\overline{XY}=18\) cm, use that to find \(\overline{YZ}\):

\[\overline{YZ}=\dfrac{2}{3}\overline{XY}=\dfrac{2}{3}(18)=12\text{ cm}\]
\[\overline{XZ}=\overline{XY}+\overline{YZ}=18+12=30\text{ cm}\]

questions.question: Points \(X\), \(Y\), and \(Z\) are on a straight line, and \(Y\) is between \(X\) and \(Z\). Length \(\overline{YZ}=\dfrac{1}{4}\overline{XY}\), and length \(\overline{XY}=28\) centimeters. What is the length of \(\overline{XZ}\)?

solution.exhibit_text:
Since \(\overline{XY}=28\) cm, use that to find \(\overline{YZ}\):

\[\overline{YZ}=\dfrac{1}{4}\overline{XY}=\dfrac{1}{4}(28)=7\text{ cm}\]
\[\overline{XZ}=\overline{XY}+\overline{YZ}=28+7=35\text{ cm}\]

questions.question: Points \(X\), \(Y\), and \(Z\) are on a straight line, and \(Y\) is between \(X\) and \(Z\). Length \(\overline{YZ}=\dfrac{5}{8}\overline{XY}\), and length \(\overline{XY}=32\) centimeters. What is the length of \(\overline{XZ}\)?

solution.exhibit_text:

\[\overline{XZ}=\overline{XY}+\overline{YZ}=32+20=52\text{ cm}\]

questions.question: Marco bought \(2\tfrac{1}{2}\) yards of fabric at $\(6.00\) per yard. If there was a \(5\%\) sales tax, what was the total cost of the fabric?

solution.exhibit_text:
Calculate the cost of the fabric before tax:

\[2\tfrac{1}{2}\times6=\dfrac{5}{2}\times6=15\]

Find the tax for $\(15\) worth of fabric:

\[15\times5\%=15\times\dfrac{5}{100}=0.75\]

Add the cost of the fabric and the tax:

\[15+0.75=15.75\]

questions.question: Jasmine bought \(3\tfrac{1}{4}\) yards of ribbon at $\(4.00\) per yard. If there was a \(10\%\) sales tax, what was the total cost of the ribbon?

solution.exhibit_text:
Calculate the cost of the ribbon before tax:

\[3\tfrac{1}{4}\times4=\dfrac{13}{4}\times4=13\]

Find the tax for $\(13\) worth of ribbon:

\[13\times10\%=13\times\dfrac{10}{100}=1.30\]

Add the cost of the ribbon and the tax:

\[13+1.30=14.30\]

questions.question: Elena bought \(1\tfrac{1}{2}\) yards of lace at $\(10.00\) per yard. If there was a \(6\%\) sales tax, what was the total cost of the lace?

solution.exhibit_text:
Calculate the cost of the lace before tax:

\[1\tfrac{1}{2}\times10=\dfrac{3}{2}\times10=15\]

Find the tax for $\(15\) worth of lace:

\[15\times6\%=15\times\dfrac{6}{100}=0.90\]

Add the cost of the lace and the tax:

\[15+0.90=15.90\]

questions.question: A piece of jewelry is made from an alloy of three metals—gold, silver, and copper—with weights in the ratio of \(5{:}3{:}2\), respectively. The piece weighs a total of \(20\) grams. What is the weight of the silver in this piece?

solution.exhibit_text:
Add the three values in the ratio (\(5+3+2=10\)) and use the sum as the denominator. Use that to find the fraction of silver in the piece: \(\dfrac{3}{10}\).

Multiply this fraction by \(20\) to find the number of grams of silver:

\[\dfrac{3}{10}\times20=6\text{ g}\]

questions.question: A trophy is made from an alloy of three metals—bronze, tin, and zinc—with weights in the ratio of \(7{:}2{:}1\), respectively. The trophy weighs a total of \(40\) grams. What is the weight of the tin in this trophy?

solution.exhibit_text:
Add the three values in the ratio (\(7+2+1=10\)) and use the sum as the denominator. Use that to find the fraction of tin in the trophy: \(\dfrac{2}{10}=\dfrac{1}{5}\).

Multiply this fraction by \(40\) to find the number of grams of tin:

\[\dfrac{1}{5}\times40=8\text{ g}\]

questions.question: A commemorative coin is made from an alloy of four metals—copper, tin, silver, and zinc—with weights in the ratio of \(9{:}4{:}3{:}2\), respectively. The coin weighs a total of \(12\) grams. What is the weight of the silver in this coin?

solution.exhibit_text:
Add the four values in the ratio (\(9+4+3+2=18\)) and use the sum as the denominator. Use that to find the fraction of silver in the coin: \(\dfrac{3}{18}=\dfrac{1}{6}\).

Multiply this fraction by \(12\) to find the number of grams of silver:

\[\dfrac{1}{6}\times12=2\text{ g}\]

questions.question: At Central High School, a survey asked two questions, Question A and Question B. For each question, students could answer either "yes" or "no." Of the \(500\) students who responded to the survey, \(450\) answered "yes" to Question A, and \(380\) answered "yes" to Question B. What is the **least** possible number of these students who could have answered "yes" to **both** questions?

solution.exhibit_text: None of the \(50\) students (\(500-450\)) who answered "no" to Question A could have answered "yes" to both questions. Therefore, the least possible number of students who could have answered "yes" to both questions can be found by subtracting the \(50\) who answered "no" to Question A from the \(380\) who answered "yes" to Question B, or \(380-50=330\).

solution.exhibit_text: None of the \(150\) students (\(1{,}000-850\)) who answered "no" to Question A could have answered "yes" to both questions. Therefore, the least possible number of students who could have answered "yes" to both questions can be found by subtracting the \(150\) who answered "no" to Question A from the \(700\) who answered "yes" to Question B, or \(700-150=550\).

solution.exhibit_text: None of the \(100\) students (\(600-500\)) who answered "no" to Question A could have answered "yes" to both questions. Therefore, the least possible number of students who could have answered "yes" to both questions can be found by subtracting the \(100\) who answered "no" to Question A from the \(460\) who answered "yes" to Question B, or \(460-100=360\).

questions.question: A wooden crate has a square base. The height of this crate is \(2\) times the length of one side of the base. If one side of the base is \(4\) feet long, what is the volume of this crate?

solution.exhibit_text: One side of the square base is \(4\) ft long. Since the height of the crate is \(2\) times the length, the height is \(2\times4=8\) ft. The volume of a rectangular prism is length \(\times\) width \(\times\) height. The volume of the crate is \(V=4\times4\times8=128\) cu ft.

questions.question: A storage bin has a square base. The height of this bin is \(4\) times the length of one side of the base. If one side of the base is \(5\) feet long, what is the volume of this bin?

solution.exhibit_text: One side of the square base is \(5\) ft long. Since the height of the bin is \(4\) times the length, the height is \(4\times5=20\) ft. The volume of a rectangular prism is length \(\times\) width \(\times\) height. The volume of the bin is \(V=5\times5\times20=500\) cu ft.

questions.question: A cardboard box has a square base. The height of this box is \(5\) times the length of one side of the base. If one side of the base is \(2\) feet long, what is the volume of this box?

solution.exhibit_text: One side of the square base is \(2\) ft long. Since the height of the box is \(5\) times the length, the height is \(5\times2=10\) ft. The volume of a rectangular prism is length \(\times\) width \(\times\) height. The volume of the box is \(V=2\times2\times10=40\) cu ft.

questions.figure_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 460 110' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' style='max-width:440px; margin: 0 auto; display: block;'><line x1='30' y1='55' x2='430' y2='55' stroke='#111' stroke-width='1.4'/><path d='M 18 55 L 33 51 L 33 59 Z' fill='#111'/><path d='M 442 55 L 427 51 L 427 59 Z' fill='#111'/><line x1='160' y1='48' x2='160' y2='62' stroke='#111' stroke-width='1.6'/><line x1='188' y1='50' x2='188' y2='60' stroke='#111' stroke-width='1'/><line x1='216' y1='50' x2='216' y2='60' stroke='#111' stroke-width='1'/><line x1='244' y1='48' x2='244' y2='62' stroke='#111' stroke-width='1.6'/><line x1='272' y1='50' x2='272' y2='60' stroke='#111' stroke-width='1'/><line x1='300' y1='48' x2='300' y2='62' stroke='#111' stroke-width='1.6'/><text x='160' y='38' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Georgia,serif' font-style='italic' font-size='16'>M</text><text x='244' y='38' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Georgia,serif' font-style='italic' font-size='16'>R</text><text x='300' y='38' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Georgia,serif' font-style='italic' font-size='16'>T</text><text x='144' y='75' font-family='Georgia,serif' font-size='13'>−</text><text x='162' y='75' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Georgia,serif' font-size='12'>3</text><line x1='155' y1='78' x2='169' y2='78' stroke='#111' stroke-width='0.8'/><text x='162' y='92' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Georgia,serif' font-size='12'>8</text><text x='300' y='75' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Georgia,serif' font-size='12'>7</text><line x1='293' y1='78' x2='307' y2='78' stroke='#111' stroke-width='0.8'/><text x='300' y='92' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Georgia,serif' font-size='12'>8</text></svg>

solution.exhibit_text:
There are \(5\) sections between \(M\) and \(T\). To find the length of one of these sections, find the distance between \(M\) and \(T\) and divide by \(5\):

\[\left(\dfrac{7}{8}-\left(-\dfrac{3}{8}\right)\right)\div\dfrac{5}{1}=\]
\[\dfrac{10}{8}\div\dfrac{5}{1}=\dfrac{10}{8}\times\dfrac{1}{5}=\dfrac{1}{4}\]

\(R\) is \(3\) sections away from \(M\), so add:

\[-\dfrac{3}{8}+3\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)=-\dfrac{3}{8}+\dfrac{6}{8}=\dfrac{3}{8}\]

\(R\) is located at \(\dfrac{3}{8}\).

solution.exhibit_text:
There are \(5\) sections between \(M\) and \(T\). To find the length of one of these sections, find the distance between \(M\) and \(T\) and divide by \(5\):

\[\left(1-\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\right)\div\dfrac{5}{1}=\]
\[\dfrac{3}{2}\div\dfrac{5}{1}=\dfrac{3}{2}\times\dfrac{1}{5}=\dfrac{3}{10}\]

\[-\dfrac{1}{2}+2\left(\dfrac{3}{10}\right)=-\dfrac{5}{10}+\dfrac{6}{10}=\dfrac{1}{10}\]

\(R\) is located at \(\dfrac{1}{10}\).

solution.exhibit_text:
There are \(5\) sections between \(M\) and \(T\). To find the length of one of these sections, find the distance between \(M\) and \(T\) and divide by \(5\):

\[\left(1\tfrac{3}{8}-\left(-\dfrac{1}{4}\right)\right)\div\dfrac{5}{1}=\]
\[\left(\dfrac{11}{8}+\dfrac{2}{8}\right)\div\dfrac{5}{1}=\dfrac{13}{8}\div\dfrac{5}{1}=\dfrac{13}{8}\times\dfrac{1}{5}=\dfrac{13}{40}\]

\(R\) is \(4\) sections away from \(M\), so add:

\[-\dfrac{1}{4}+4\left(\dfrac{13}{40}\right)=-\dfrac{10}{40}+\dfrac{52}{40}=\dfrac{42}{40}=1\tfrac{1}{20}\]

\(R\) is located at \(1\tfrac{1}{20}\).
